explanations.explanation: Mark 4:36 says the disciples took Jesus with them "…since He was already in the boat." So nobody had to fetch Him. They dismissed the crowd, and Jesus was already aboard. The boat was ready with Him in it.

explanations.answer: He joins them at the dock
explanations.explanation: No dock in this passage, friend. Mark 4:36 says they took Jesus with them "…since He was already in the boat." The text puts Him aboard already. Nobody had to meet Him anywhere.

explanations.answer: He wades out to meet them
explanations.explanation: Wading out sounds like a dramatic entrance, but that's not what happens. Mark 4:36 says they took Jesus with them "…since He was already in the boat." He was already aboard when they took Him along. No wading needed.
Yes, ma'am, yes, sir. Mark 4:36 says, "And there were other boats with Him." So this was a little fleet, not a lone boat. The text doesn't tell us who was in those other boats, and I won't guess.

It's actually true. Mark 4:36 says, "And there were other boats with Him." The disciples weren't the only boat out on that water. The text doesn't say who, if anyone, was aboard those other boats, so I'll leave that one alone.
Mark 4:37 says the waves were breaking over the boat, "…so that it was being swamped." That's more water coming in than the boat can handle. I bet anybody on board wished they were somewhere calmer.

An anchor is for holding a boat in place, and that's not the word here. Mark 4:37 says the waves were breaking over it, "…so that it was being swamped." Swamped means filling with water. I think an anchor would have been the least of their worries.

Steering sounds like somebody's in charge of the situation. Mark 4:37 says the waves were breaking over the boat, "…so that it was being swamped." That's the word. The water was the one doing the taking over, not the people.
Not quite, friend. Mark 4:38 says, "So they woke Him…" They did not tiptoe around the sleeping Teacher. They went and got Him up, and then they asked Him a question.

Right, they didn't let Him sleep. Mark 4:38 says, "So they woke Him and said, 'Teacher, don't You care that we are perishing?'" Jesus was in the stern on the cushion, and the disciples went straight to Him. I think I would have done the same, and probably a lot louder.

explanations.answer: Whether He cares that they're perishing
explanations.explanation: Mark 4:38 has them say, "Teacher, don’t You care that we are perishing?" They woke Him and asked it straight. That's a question you ask when the water is coming in and you're scared. I think it was the loudest question that boat ever heard.

explanations.answer: Whether they should turn back to shore
explanations.explanation: Nobody asks about turning back in this passage. In Mark 4:38 they say, "Teacher, don’t You care that we are perishing?" It's a question about Jesus Himself, not about the route. The text doesn't mention shore at all.

explanations.answer: Whether He can help them row
explanations.explanation: Rowing never comes up, friend. Mark 4:38 has them say, "Teacher, don’t You care that we are perishing?" They didn't ask for a spare set of hands. They asked Him whether He cared.
Mark 4:39 says Jesus "…rebuked the wind and the sea." Then He told them, "Silence!" and "Be still!" He spoke to the wind and the water directly. And they listened.
Rain isn't in this passage at all. Mark 4:39 says Jesus "…rebuked the wind and the sea." The storm in Mark 4:37 is called a violent windstorm, and the wind is what He addressed.
No clouds in the text, friend. Mark 4:39 says Jesus "…rebuked the wind and the sea." Those are the two He spoke to. I'll leave the weather forecasting to somebody else.

explanations.answer: The wind dies down and it's perfectly calm
explanations.explanation: Mark 4:39 says, "And the wind died down, and it was perfectly calm." That came after He commanded, "Silence!" and "Be still!" No leftover wind is mentioned. A violent windstorm turned into perfectly calm.

explanations.answer: The waves stop but the wind keeps blowing
explanations.explanation: The text doesn't split it up like that. Mark 4:39 says, "And the wind died down, and it was perfectly calm." The wind died down, and the whole scene went calm with it.

explanations.answer: The storm slowly fades through the night
explanations.explanation: The text doesn't describe a slow fade. Mark 4:39 says Jesus commanded the wind and sea, "And the wind died down, and it was perfectly calm." There's no mention of it lasting through the night. It went from violent to perfectly calm after He spoke.
Mark 4:40 has Jesus ask, "Why are you so afraid?" That's His first question. The second one comes right behind it. It came after the sea was already calm.

explanations.answer: Why did you wake Me up
explanations.explanation: Jesus never says that. In Mark 4:40 He asks, "Why are you so afraid?" Not a word about the wake-up call. I think I would have grumbled a little, but that's me and my snooze button.

explanations.answer: Why didn't you steer for shore
explanations.explanation: Steering never comes up. Mark 4:40 has Jesus ask, "Why are you so afraid?" His question is about their fear, not their navigation.

Mark 4:40 has Jesus ask, "Do you still have no faith?" That's His second question, right after "Why are you so afraid?" Two questions, back to back. I think it's a question worth sitting with, friend.
Wisdom is a good thing, but it's not the word here. Mark 4:40 has Jesus ask, "Do you still have no faith?" He's asking about faith, not wisdom.
I get why you'd pick it, with all that water. But Mark 4:40 has Jesus ask, "Do you still have no faith?" Faith is the word, not patience.

explanations.answer: Who is this that even the wind and the sea obey Him
explanations.explanation: Mark 4:41 says, "Who is this, that even the wind and the sea obey Him?" They said it overwhelmed with fear. The sea was calm, and the fear was still there. The text doesn't answer the question right there, so I'll leave it hanging too.

explanations.answer: How are we ever going to get back to the shore
explanations.explanation: The text never has them ask that. In Mark 4:41 they ask, "Who is this, that even the wind and the sea obey Him?" Their question is about Jesus, not about the trip home.

explanations.answer: Where did such a terrible storm come from so fast
explanations.explanation: That's a fair thing to wonder, but it's not what they say. Mark 4:41 has them ask, "Who is this, that even the wind and the sea obey Him?" Their eyes were on Jesus, not on the weather report.
